title: There was a puzzle game I loved as a kid but could never keep playing, so I spent 11 months building my own with AI coding agents
author: benkigera
selftext:
Solo dev from Kenya. I'm not a game dev by trade, and this is my first released game. Focus Rail is a calm train-routing puzzle: coloured trains leave the tunnel and you flip the switches so each one reaches the house that matches its colour. The video is level 7 played through.

Stack: Flutter + Flame, about 220 commits since November 2025. Almost all the code was written by AI coding agents. The art is procedural code too (trains, houses and the tree tunnel are drawn in code), no image or audio generators.

What actually mattered:

1. **One rules file the agents read every session.** The biggest jump in quality came from writing down where the truth lives: level topology → layout lattice → rail geometry → rails, switches, houses and trains. Before that, agents "fixed" ugly boards by nudging coordinates or even editing level files, and every fix broke something else.

2. **Agents copy whatever shortcut is already in the code.** An old hard-coded 50-pixel grid kept coming back in new components until I made the lattice the only thing allowed to place anything.

3. **Name the effect you want, not the fix.** Trains used to snap between sprites when they turned. "Make the turn smoother" got me tweens. "Each car is a small 3D model that yaws to its own rail tangent, with the camera angle driven by that tangent" got me a train that actually turns through bends.

4. **I banned unit tests for this project.** The agents kept writing tests that passed while the game looked wrong. Now every feature build goes to Play internal testing and I play it on my phone.

5. **Keep a roadmap file the agent updates in the same commit as the work.** It stops it marking things "done" that only exist in a plan.

It's free on Android (3 lives a day and optional ads, I'm being upfront). Happy to share the rules file or go deeper on the rail geometry if anyone's fighting the same "AI keeps breaking layout" problem.
